subject.title: Chronic agent failures on Telegram — LLM timeouts before configured timeout + silent incomplete turns + dead fallbacks (OpenRouter/DeepSeek+V4-Flash, v2026.5.28)

question: Is the v2026.5.28 diagnostic bundle enough to choose a code fix, or should maintainers require a current-release Telegram/OpenRouter repro with effective provider timeout config before narrowing this issue?
rationale: Current main has related component fixes, but the observable composite failure depends on provider config and live provider/channel behavior that source inspection alone cannot prove against the reporter's setup.

options.title: Require current-run proof
options.body: Ask for one current-release Telegram/OpenRouter runId trace with effective `models.providers.openrouter.timeoutSeconds`, fallback logs, and Telegram delivery evidence before assigning a code fix.

options.title: Triage to timeout config/docs
options.body: Treat the report primarily as a provider-timeout configuration mismatch and clarify the required provider-level timeout path, accepting that the original live failure remains unproven.

options.title: Sponsor a live repro
options.body: A maintainer runs a comparable Telegram/OpenRouter live repro and uses that to split any confirmed timeout, fallback, or delivery fixes into narrower issues.

recommendation.title: Require current-run proof
recommendation.body: Ask for one current-release Telegram/OpenRouter runId trace with effective `models.providers.openrouter.timeoutSeconds`, fallback logs, and Telegram delivery evidence before assigning a code fix.

likelyOwner.reason: The most load-bearing unresolved proof question is whether the reporter's setup uses the provider-level timeout path that recent timeout work owns.
